findings.title: Google Meet booking with no destination calendar throws TypeError
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` gives `undefined` when the array is empty or null. `handleNewBooking` sends `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067), and the other callers send `[]`. When the location is Google Meet, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws, so the booking fails. Before this change the code fell back to Cal Video here. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Org slug condition is inverted
findings.body: The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`: the slug was set right away only when billing is disabled, and when billing is enabled it was kept in `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment (features/ee/teams/api/upgrade.ts:45 publishes from `requestedSlug`). The new `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` flips this. With billing enabled, the org is published with its slug before anyone pays. With billing disabled (self-hosted), the org is created with no slug and no `requestedSlug`, so nothing can ever publish it. This rewrite is not part of the calendar change. Restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` on line 151.

findings.title: Video references lose their credentialId
findings.body: The old code saved `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results. Now it saves `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so every `_video` booking reference is stored without a credentialId. Later updates and deletes of the video meeting that look up the credential by `reference.credentialId` then fall back or fail. Keep `result.credentialId` for both kinds of result.

findings.title: Non-Google calendars always write to the first host's calendar id
findings.body: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now calls `createEvent(credential, event, ...)` once per host, each time with that host's credential and the full `destinationCalendar` array. Only Google uses the passed `credentialId` to pick its own entry. Office365 (this line), Lark (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:128) and CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-163) always take `destinationCalendar[0]`, which is the main host's calendar. A second collective host on Outlook gets a request to `/me/calendars/<host1 id>/events` under their own token, which fails. A CalDAV host's calendar list is filtered down to nothing. Either way the second host gets no event. Pick the entry whose `credentialId` matches the credential, as Google does, or use the `externalId` that `CalendarManager.createEvent` now receives.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback can never match
findings.body: This branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and then it looks for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, so it never finds a real calendar. Before, the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. In `updateEvent`, `calendarId` is now `undefined` and the Google API rejects the call. In `deleteEvent` (line 317) the code falls back to `primary`, which deletes from the wrong calendar. This hits references saved without `externalCalendarId`: older bookings, and, after this PR, every event created through the no-credentialId path in `createAllCalendarEvents` (EventManager.ts:376-381), because `createEvent` is called there without an `externalId`. Fall back to the destination calendar whose `credentialId` matches this credential, or to the first entry.

findings.title: Team members' calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
findings.body: If neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (line 1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so the other collective hosts' calendars are thrown away without any sign. Initialise it to `[]` and push into that.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation repeats per reference and skips other hosts
findings.body: The recurring branch now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. For every calendar reference it goes through all of the organizer's calendar credentials and deletes `updBooking.references.find(...)`, which is always the first calendar reference. With N host references, the organizer's event is deleted N times, and the other hosts' recurring events are never deleted, because only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` is used and only the first ref of each booking is looked at. Run the recurring deletion once, outside the loop, over every `_calendar` reference of each booking, using each reference's own credential.

findings.title: Member calendars without credentialId end up on the organizer's credentials
findings.body: When a pushed team member's `destinationCalendar` has no `credentialId`, `createAllCalendarEvents` takes the else branch (EventManager.ts:376-381). That branch filters `this.calendarCredentials`, which are the organizer's credentials, by integration type, so it creates a second copy of the event in the organizer's calendar instead of the member's. Consider skipping such entries for non-organizer hosts, or resolving that member's credentials.

findings.title: loadUsers turns validation errors into a 500
findings.body: An empty `dynamicUserList` now throws a plain `Error`. The catch block turns that into `HttpError(500, "Unable to load users")`, while before the code returned an empty list and handled it downstream. `error instanceof HttpError` can never be true inside this try block. Also, the `organization.slug` select was removed from the dynamic-user query, but `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 355) still declares it.
